title: Development and validation of a red-edge-based index for improving satellite detection of algal blooms in inland waters

title: A CNN-based mapping approach for aeolian dunes in Arctic Sweden
abstract: Aeolian dunes provide valuable evidence of past wind regimes and environmental change but mapping them reliably over large areas remains challenging. Manual delineation of dune boundaries is time-consuming and difficult to apply consistently. Automated approaches also struggle where vegetation partly obscures dune morphology and where sand-rich fluvial surfaces, such as riverbanks and terraces, exhibit spectral responses similar to those of stabilized dunes. In this study, dune mapping is treated as a pixel-wise binary segmentation task that separates dune-covered areas, including adjoining or overlapping dunes, from the surrounding background. We present ArcticSandNet, a multimodal segmentation network based on the U-Net architecture. Optical imagery and terrain variables derived from a digital elevation model (DEM), including elevation, slope, and curvature, are processed by two separate encoders. Their features are combined at each encoder level through feature concatenation. In the decoder, an attention-based module fuses encoder skips features with upsampled decoder features, helping the network retain dune-related spatial information while suppressing responses from heterogeneous background surfaces. The model was trained and evaluated across 15 sites in northern Sweden using spatial five-fold cross-validation. A further site was excluded from all model training, validation, and selection procedures and retained solely for independent testing. In cross-validation, ArcticSandNet achieved a two-class mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 78.15% ± 5.34% and a two-class mean F1 score (mF1) of 85.97% ± 4.78%. For the dune class, it achieved an F1 score of 72.61% ± 8.46% and an IoU of 57.63% ± 9.59%, outperforming U-Net, SegNet, and Attention U-Net trained under the same settings. On the independent test site, ArcticSandNet achieved a dune-class recall of 60.52%, an F1 score of 67.16%, and an IoU of 50.55%, also outperforming the three benchmark networks in dune-class F1 and IoU. The resulting maps of dune-covered areas provide a consistent spatial basis for regional analyses of dune-field characteristics, morphology, and landscape stability.

title: A Metro-InSAR Risk Index for corridor-scale displacement risk diagnosis of urban rail infrastructure
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Time-series Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) provides dense displacement observations along urban rail corridors, yet converting point-based measurements into corridor-scale diagnostic information remains challenging. This study proposes the Metro-InSAR Risk Index (MIRI), a diagnostic index designed to convert multi-dimensional InSAR-derived displacement characteristics into displacement-related diagnostic levels for urban metro corridors. MIRI integrates displacement rate, cumulative displacement, local displacement heterogeneity, height-related variability, and temporal residual variability, thereby extending conventional velocity-based interpretation toward corridor-scale displacement-risk diagnosis. The framework was applied to the Kunming Metro Network using 198 descending Sentinel-1 images acquired from March 2018 to December 2024. The time-series InSAR results show that the network was generally stable, with line-of-sight (LOS) displacement rates mainly ranging from −6 to 3 mm/yr and 97.21% of coherent scatterers falling within the stable interval of −3 to 3 mm/yr. Localized displacement anomalies were mainly observed near line intersections, curved sections, construction-affected areas, and the Dianchi Lake shoreline. Based on MIRI, 78%, 17%, 4%, and 1% of valid points were classified as Levels D, C, B, and A, respectively, indicating a distribution dominated by lower diagnostic levels, with spatially confined Level-B and Level-A anomalies particularly along Lines 4 and 5 and in lakeside soft-ground areas. Multi-source contextual variables and XGBoost-SHAP analysis were further used to interpret the environmental, anthropogenic, operational, and displacement-gradient information associated with the MIRI-based diagnostic patterns. The results indicate that the spatial variation in MIRI is mainly associated with terrain-related conditions, corridor-scale displacement variation, metro operation, and urban development intensity. By deriving diagnostic levels directly from PSI-based displacement indicators, MIRI provides an InSAR-based screening tool for prioritizing displacement-related anomalies and supporting maintenance of urban rail transit systems.

title: Removal notice to “Optimized gated spatiotemporal graph attention network based diagnosis of facial expression through video games” [Pattern Recognition 175 (2026) 112991]
Long-form Video-to-Text Summarization using Recursive Language Models
abstract: While VideoLLMs have made significant progress in understanding short video benchmarks, they often struggle to summarize long-form ones. This is mainly due to performance degradation caused by long-context prompts, the inherent difficulty of preserving temporal continuity and a lack of semantically rich concepts in event descriptions. To tackle these issues, this paper introduces the first recursive Video Language Summarization Model (RVLSM) designed for video processing and tailored to long-form video-to-text summarization. RVLSM recursively decomposes videos into semantically coherent segments and delegates chunk-level reasoning to VideoLLM sub-models and external tools. It employs (1) Semantic Temporal Decomposition (STD), which preserves temporal coherence and continuity through a scene-aware chunking strategy that dynamically partitions videos according to semantic boundaries, and (2) Adaptive Multimodal Tool Calling (AMTC), which ensures semantic richness of the summary via a routing mechanism that selectively invokes auxiliary modules such as action recognition, optical character recognition, automatic speech recognition, and object detection. Experiments on the VideoXum and MixTyVSum benchmarks show that RVLSM consistently improves over zero-shot VideoLLM baselines across multiple model settings and performance metrics, and is competitive with a state-of-the-art fine-tuned model for video-to-text summarization. Importantly, the named entities in the RVLSM's summaries align more closely with those detected in the ground-truth summaries than those detected by baseline and state-of-the-art methods, confirming the saliency of the event descriptions it generates.

title: Quantifying Uncertainty Bounds in Spectral Shallow Water Bathymetry: The Profile Likelihood Framework for Semi-Analytical Models
abstract:
Accurate bathymetric mapping in shallow waters is critical for coastal monitoring, navigation safety, and environmental conservation. While semi-analytical (SA) models have proven effective for estimating water column depth (WCD) from optical remote sensing data, quantifying the associated uncertainties remains a significant challenge. This study introduces a unified framework based on profile likelihood to evaluate WCD uncertainties in Semi-Analytical (SA) models, bridging traditional variance-covariance methods with likelihood-based inference. Through controlled simulations, we systematically assess the performance of first-order statistical tests-likelihood ratio, Wald (observed and expected), and score tests-across varying environmental conditions and sensor configurations.

Our results demonstrate that the expected Fisher information Wald test, equivalent to classical variance-covariance propagation, provides reliable uncertainty bounds in hyperspectral settings with clear waters. However, its performance deteriorates in multispectral applications and complex water conditions, where likelihood ratio tests prove more robust. This divergence highlights fundamental limitations in the small-sample regime typical of per-pixel spectral bathymetry. Notably, even under idealized conditions with true parameter initialization, local optimization challenges in SA models can compromise both parameter estimation and uncertainty quantification, suggesting even greater challenges in practical applications with less favorable initialization. The findings underscore the importance of robust statistical inference in improving the reliability of bathymetric products for operational applications.

title: Data-Efficient Learning from Demonstration for Humanoid Robots via Feature-Level Perception and Prompt-Based Object Detection
abstract: Learning from Demonstration (LfD) allows robots to learn new skills from human examples; however, many vision-based methods require large datasets and resource-intensive end-to-end training. This paper introduces a data-efficient LfD framework for humanoid robots that learns manipulation skills from compact, task-specific features instead of raw images. The proposed approach integrates layered visual preprocessing, Kinect-based human joint estimation, prompt-based object detection, and depth information to extract human motion features and three-dimensional object locations from demonstration videos. These features are used to train a temporal deep learning model that predicts robot joint-angle trajectories for execution. The framework is implemented on a NAO humanoid robot, evaluated quantitatively in simulation, and demonstrated on physical hardware. In simulation, the robot achieves a 78% success rate on a pick-and-place task using only 16 demonstrations, which increases to 86% when trained with 100 demonstrations. The framework also achieves a 71% success rate on a pushing task using eight demonstrations, highlighting its effectiveness for data-efficient humanoid skill acquisition.
